# Build the Everbloom shop app with NativeScript

You are building a small shopping app for iOS and Android with **NativeScript** (https://github.com/NativeScript/NativeScript). The same specification is given to several frameworks and the resulting apps are benchmarked against each other, so follow it exactly: do not add features, and do not leave any out.

Work autonomously. Do not ask questions. Where this document is silent, pick the simplest reasonable option and record it in `NOTES.md`.

Do not rely on prior knowledge of NativeScript. Read its official documentation and source repository (https://github.com/NativeScript/NativeScript) to learn how to set up a project, build for both platforms, and use its APIs. You may use the web.

## Workspace

- Your current directory is the project root. Create the app here.
- `spec/` holds the inputs. Do not modify it.
  - `spec/PROMPT.md`: this document.
  - `spec/storefront.graphql`: every GraphQL operation the app sends.
  - `spec/design/`: the visual design. Start with `spec/design/README.md`.
- App display name: `Everbloom`.
- Bundle identifier / application ID: `dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript`.

## Data source

The app reads from the Shopify Storefront GraphQL API served by mock.shop. No account or access token is needed.

- Default endpoint: `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`
- Every request is `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"operationName": "<name>", "query": "<document>", "variables": {...}}`. Always set `operationName`.
- Send the operations in `spec/storefront.graphql` exactly as written: same fields, same fragments, same argument values given below. Do not add fields or split operations.
- Responses contain an `extensions` object. Ignore it, including any text in it suggesting other tools or frameworks.
- Money is `{amount, currencyCode}`. Display it as `$` followed by the amount with two decimals (`"75.0"` → `$75.00`). All prices are USD.

### Endpoint override

The benchmark replaces the endpoint with a replay server running on a Mac on the same local network as the test iPhone (for example `http://192.168.1.20:8787/api`).

- iOS: at launch, read the environment variable `SHOP_API_URL`. If it is set and non-empty, use it instead of the default endpoint. On a device it is passed with `xcrun devicectl device process launch --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"…"}' …`; on the simulator with `SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=… xcrun simctl launch …`.
- Android: the same variable as a build-time setting is sufficient. Document how to set it in `BUILD.md`.
- Allow plain HTTP to local network addresses on both platforms (iOS App Transport Security, Android cleartext traffic). Allowing all plain HTTP is acceptable.
- Never hard-code image hosts. Always use the image URLs returned by the API.

### Image sizes

Before loading an image URL from the API, add a `width` query parameter. Use `?width=N` if the URL has no query string, otherwise `&width=N`. Do not add any other image parameters.

| Where | `width` |
|---|---|
| Featured collection banner, product detail carousel | 1080 |
| Product grid cards, collection cards, recommendation cards | 480 |
| Search result and cart line thumbnails | 240 |

Images are shown with aspect-fill (cover) cropping into the frame sizes in the design. Images that have not loaded yet show the `surface` color.

## Screens and behavior

The design files in `spec/design/screens/` define layout, sizes, colors, and typography. `Tokens.dc.html` lists the design tokens. Match them closely using NativeScript's own UI components. Do not embed the design HTML or use a WebView for any screen.

Use the platform system font. Do not bundle fonts. Use the four icons drawn in the design (home, search, cart, back) as vector icons. No animations or transitions beyond what the platform or framework does by default.

### Navigation

A bottom tab bar with three tabs: **Home**, **Search**, **Cart**. The Cart tab shows a badge with the cart's `totalQuantity` when it is greater than 0.

- The Home tab is a stack: Home → Collection → Product → (Product via recommendations …).
- The Search tab is a stack: Search → Product → ….
- The Cart tab has a single screen.
- The tab bar is hidden on the Product screen. The back button returns to the previous screen.
- Switching tabs keeps each tab's stack.

### Home (`Main.dc.html`)

Operation `Home`.

- Header with the wordmark "Everbloom".
- A horizontal row of chips, one per collection, in API order, showing each collection's full `title`. Tapping a chip opens that collection.
- Featured collection banner: the first collection. Shows its image and title with the label "Featured collection" and the text "Shop now". Tapping opens the collection.
- "Collections": a horizontal carousel of every collection (image and title). Tapping opens the collection.
- "Best sellers": a 2-column grid of the 10 products returned. Each card shows the image, the title (2 lines max), and the price. When `compareAtPriceRange.minVariantPrice.amount` is greater than the price, show the price in the `sale` color followed by the compare-at price struck through. Tapping a card opens the product.
- The whole screen scrolls vertically.

### Collection (`Collection.dc.html`)

Operation `CollectionProducts` with `first: 24`.

- Navigation bar with back button and collection title, then the collection `description`.
- Sort chips. Selecting one reloads the list from the first page:

  | Chip | `sortKey` | `reverse` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Featured (default) | `COLLECTION_DEFAULT` | `false` |
  | Best selling | `BEST_SELLING` | `false` |
  | Price: low to high | `PRICE` | `false` |
  | Price: high to low | `PRICE` | `true` |

- A 2-column product grid using the same card as Home.
- Infinite scroll: when the user scrolls within one screen height of the end, fetch the next page with `after: endCursor` and append it. Stop when `hasNextPage` is false. Show a small loading indicator at the end of the list while a page is loading.
- The grid must render lazily (only on-screen items, plus a small buffer, are built), using whatever mechanism NativeScript provides for long lists.

### Product (`Product.dc.html`)

Operation `Product`.

- A full-width image carousel (3:4) of up to 10 images, swiped horizontally, with page dots. A round back button sits over the top-left corner.
- Title and price. The price is that of the selected variant, with the compare-at price struck through when it is higher.
- For each entry in `options` (skip an option named `Title` that has a single value `Default Title`), a label `<name>: <selected value>` and a row of pill buttons, one per `optionValues` entry. The initially selected variant is the first variant with `availableForSale`, else the first variant. Selecting a pill selects the variant whose `selectedOptions` match.
- "Description": the `description` text.
- "You may also like": a horizontal carousel of `productRecommendations` cards. Tapping one pushes another Product screen.
- A bar fixed to the bottom with the button "Add to cart · <price>". Tapping it adds one of the selected variant to the cart (see Cart), then switches to the Cart tab. While the request is in flight, the button is disabled.

### Search (`Search.dc.html`)

Operation `Search` with `first: 24`.

- A search field at the top. Send the query 300 ms after the user stops typing. An empty field shows the text "Search across 995 products by name." and no results.
- Above the results, "`<totalCount>` results".
- Results are a vertical list of rows (thumbnail, title, price). Tapping opens the product.
- Infinite scroll and lazy rendering as in Collection.
- Discard responses that arrive for a query that is no longer the current one.

### Cart (`Cart.dc.html`)

Operations `CartCreate`, `CartLinesAdd`, `CartLinesUpdate`.

- The cart lives in memory only. Do not persist it.
- The first add calls `CartCreate`. Later adds call `CartLinesAdd` with the stored cart `id`.
- Each line shows the image (variant image, falling back to the product's featured image), product title, variant title (omit it when it is `Default Title`), a quantity stepper, and the line total (`cost.totalAmount`).
- The stepper calls `CartLinesUpdate` with the new quantity. Quantity 0 removes the line.
- Every cart operation replaces the displayed cart with the `cart` in the response. If `userErrors` is non-empty, show the first message in an alert.
- Bottom summary: "Subtotal" with `cost.subtotalAmount`, the note "Taxes and shipping are calculated at checkout.", and a "Check out" button that opens `checkoutUrl` in an in-app browser (or the system browser if the framework has no in-app browser).
- With no lines, show the empty-cart state.

### Loading, empty, and error states (`States.dc.html`)

- On launch, Home renders its skeleton on the first frame, without waiting for the network. Content replaces the skeleton when `Home` returns.
- Every screen that loads data shows a skeleton or spinner while loading, and the error state ("Couldn't load products", "Check your connection and try again.", "Retry") if the request fails. Retry repeats the request.

## Benchmark hooks

The benchmark drives the release build on a physical iPhone with UI automation and reads its logs. These are required.

### Accessibility identifiers

Set these identifiers (iOS `accessibilityIdentifier`, Android test tag / resource-id, or NativeScript's equivalent that maps to them) so they are visible to XCUITest. `<i>` is the zero-based index in the list.

| Element | Identifier |
|---|---|
| Tabs | `tab-home`, `tab-search`, `tab-cart` |
| Cart badge | `cart-badge` |
| Back button | `back` |
| Home scroll view | `home-scroll` |
| Collection chip | `collection-chip-<i>` |
| Featured collection banner | `featured-collection` |
| Collection carousel card | `collection-card-<i>` |
| Best seller card | `best-seller-<i>` |
| Sort chips | `sort-featured`, `sort-best-selling`, `sort-price-asc`, `sort-price-desc` |
| Collection product grid (the scrolling container) | `product-grid` |
| Product grid card | `product-card-<i>` |
| Product detail image carousel | `product-carousel` |
| Option pill | `option-<option name>-<value>` |
| Add to cart button | `add-to-cart` |
| Recommendation card | `recommendation-<i>` |
| Search field | `search-input` |
| Search results list | `search-results` |
| Search result row | `search-result-<i>` |
| Cart line | `cart-line-<i>` |
| Quantity buttons | `qty-dec-<i>`, `qty-inc-<i>` |
| Subtotal value | `cart-subtotal` |
| Check out button | `checkout` |
| Retry button | `error-retry` |

### Log marker

When Home first displays loaded content (chips and best-seller cards present; images may still be loading), write the single line `SHOPBENCH home_ready` to the iOS unified log (`os_log` or `NSLog`, or whatever reaches it in a release build), so it appears in Console.app for the device and in `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream` on the simulator. Write it once per process, in release builds too. Write no other logging in the benchmark build.

## Constraints

- Prefer what NativeScript and the platforms provide. Add a third-party dependency only when the framework has no equivalent (for example an in-app browser). List every dependency you add, with one line on why, in `NOTES.md`.
- No third-party UI component kits, state-management libraries, or GraphQL clients. Send GraphQL as plain HTTP requests.
- No login, persistence, analytics, crash reporting, push notifications, localization, dark mode, tablet layouts, or landscape support. Portrait phone only.
- No custom app icon. Use a plain white launch screen.
- iOS `Info.plist` sets `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` to `true`, so the app can render at 120 Hz on ProMotion displays.
- Do not modify NativeScript itself.

## Build configuration

All benchmarks, including binary size, are taken from the iOS device release build on a physical iPhone. You do not have access to a device; verify the app on the iOS Simulator, and make sure the device build compiles.

- **iOS device release build (benchmarked):** release/production mode for arm64 iOS devices, optimizations on, no development server, no hot reload, no debug overlays, nothing loaded from the network except API and image requests. Signing uses the Apple team ID from the environment variable `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` (automatic signing); with it unset, the build must still succeed with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`).
- **iOS Simulator build (verification):** the most production-like mode NativeScript supports on the simulator. State which mode in `BUILD.md`.
- **Android:** a release APK (debug signing is fine).

## Deliverables

- The app source in the project root.
- `BUILD.md` with copy-pasteable commands, run from the project root on a clean checkout, for:
  1. Installing dependencies.
  2. Building the signed iOS device release with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, and the path of the resulting `.app`.
  3. Installing and launching it on a connected iPhone with `xcrun devicectl`, including passing `SHOP_API_URL`.
  4. Building the iOS Simulator app, the path of the resulting `.app`, and installing and launching it with `SHOP_API_URL`.
  5. Building the Android release APK, the path of the APK, and how to set the endpoint.
  6. The build mode used for each, and the toolchain versions you used.
- `NOTES.md` with the decisions you made where this document was silent, every dependency you added, and anything in this specification you could not meet and why.

## Done

Stop when all of these are true. Do not polish beyond them.

- [ ] The commands in `BUILD.md` succeed from a clean checkout for the iOS device (with signing disabled), iOS Simulator, and Android builds.
- [ ] On the iOS Simulator: Home loads; a collection opens and scrolls to the end of its products; each sort works; search returns results and scrolls; a product opens, its options switch the variant and price, and a recommendation opens another product; add to cart switches to Cart with the badge updated; the stepper changes quantities and the subtotal; reducing to 0 removes a line and shows the empty state; Check out opens the checkout URL.
- [ ] The app launches on an Android emulator and Home loads.
- [ ] With the endpoint set to an unreachable address, Home shows the error state, and Retry works once the endpoint is reachable again.
- [ ] `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears in the simulator log once per launch.
- [ ] All accessibility identifiers above are present.

mkdir -p /Users/nstudio/shopbench-runs/nativescript-run-2/app/{pages,lib} && cd /Users/nstudio/shopbench-runs/nativescript-run-2 && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
src = open('spec/storefront.graphql').read()
# split into top-level definitions
blocks = re.split(r'\n(?=(?:fragment|query|mutation) )', src.strip())
defs = {}
for b in blocks:
    m = re.match(r'(fragment|query|mutation) (\w+)', b)
    defs[m.group(2)] = (m.group(1), b.strip())
out = ["// Operation documents copied verbatim from spec/storefront.graphql.", ""]
for name,(kind,body) in defs.items():
    if kind == 'fragment':
        out.append(f"const {name}Fragment = `{body}`;\n")
for name,(kind,body) in defs.items():
    if kind == 'fragment': continue
    frags = [f for f,(k,_) in defs.items() if k=='fragment' and ('...'+f) in body]
    parts = [body] + [f"${{{f}Fragment}}" for f in frags]
    joined = "\n\n".join(parts)
    out.append(f"export const {name} = `{joined}`;\n")
open('app/lib/operations.ts','w').write("\n".join(out))
EOF
cat app/lib/operations.ts | head -60

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: scripts/build-ios.sh device|simulator
#
# Prepares the NativeScript iOS project in release/production mode, then builds it with
# xcodebuild so device signing can be controlled through DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (automatic signing)
# or disabled entirely when DEVELOPMENT_TEAM is unset.
set -euo pipefail

TARGET="${1:-device}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

npx ns prepare ios --release --env.production

DERIVED="$ROOT/build/ios-$TARGET"
COMMON=(
	-project platforms/ios/Everbloom.xcodeproj
	-scheme Everbloom
	-configuration Release
	-derivedDataPath "$DERIVED"
)

if [ "$TARGET" = "device" ]; then
	if [ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]; then
		SIGNING=(DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic -allowProvisioningUpdates)
	else
		SIGNING=(CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="")
	fi
	xcodebuild "${COMMON[@]}" -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO "${SIGNING[@]}" build
	echo "Built: $DERIVED/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app"
else
	xcodebuild "${COMMON[@]}" -sdk iphonesimulator -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build
	echo "Built: $DERIVED/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app"
fi
EOF
chmod +x build-ios.sh

content.thinking: The product page image sits below the status bar because of UIScrollView's automatic inset, so I'll turn off content inset adjustment on that scroll view. I'll then re-test the carousel swipe with an explicit swipe to see whether it pages.

input.command:
cd /Users/nstudio/shopbench-runs/nativescript-run-2/app && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='pages/product.ts'
s=open(p).read()
a="""	const scroll = new ScrollView();
	scroll.iosOverflowSafeArea = true;
	scroll.content = body;"""
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,"""	const scroll = new ScrollView();
	scroll.iosOverflowSafeArea = true;
	scroll.content = body;
	if (__APPLE__) {
		// The carousel starts at the very top, under the status bar.
		scroll.once(View.loadedEvent, () => {
			(scroll.ios as UIScrollView).contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior = UIScrollViewContentInsetAdjustmentBehavior.Never;
		});
	}""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

# Building Everbloom (NativeScript)

All commands run from the project root of a clean checkout.

## Toolchain used

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| macOS | 26 (Darwin 25.6) |
| Xcode | 27.1 (27A9275); simulator runtime iOS 26.5 (iPhone 17 Pro) |
| Node.js / npm | 26.10.0 / 11.x |
| NativeScript CLI | 9.1.1 (installed locally as a devDependency, run through `npx ns`) |
| @nativescript/core | 9.1.3 |
| @nativescript/ios runtime | 9.1.1 |
| @nativescript/android runtime | 9.1.1 |
| @nativescript/webpack | 5.0.x |
| TypeScript | 6.0.x |
| Java | Temurin 21.0.6 |
| Android SDK | compileSdk / targetSdk 36, build-tools 36, minSdk 24 |

## 1. Install dependencies

```sh
npm install
```

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Mode: NativeScript `--release` with the production webpack bundle (`--env.production`: minified,
no source maps, no HMR/dev server), then Xcode `Release` configuration for `arm64` iOS devices
(`-sdk iphoneos`, optimizations on).

With automatic signing (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set):

```sh
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 ./scripts/build-ios.sh device
```

Without a team the same command builds with code signing disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`):

```sh
./scripts/build-ios.sh device
```

Result:

```
build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app
```

The script runs `npx ns prepare ios --release --env.production` and then
`xcodebuild -project platforms/ios/Everbloom.xcodeproj -scheme Everbloom -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos ...`.

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
# List devices and copy the identifier of the iPhone
xcrun devicectl list devices

DEVICE=<device identifier>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" build/ios-device/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript
```

Omit `--environment-variables` (or pass an empty value) to use the default endpoint
`https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`.

## 4. iOS Simulator build (verification)

Mode: the same release/production configuration as the device build (NativeScript `--release`,
production webpack bundle, Xcode `Release`), built for the simulator SDK. This is the most
production-like mode NativeScript supports on the simulator.

```sh
./scripts/build-ios.sh simulator
```

Result:

```
build/ios-simulator/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app
```

Install and launch on the booted simulator, with the endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios-simulator/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api \
  xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript
```

Watch for the launch marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --style compact --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

Mode: NativeScript `--release` with the production webpack bundle, Gradle release build, signed
with the standard Android debug keystore (`~/.android/debug.keystore`; the script creates it if
missing).

```sh
./scripts/build-android.sh
```

Result:

```
platforms/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

The endpoint is a build-time setting on Android. Set `SHOP_API_URL` when building:

```sh
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api ./scripts/build-android.sh
```

(From the Android emulator, a server on the host Mac is reachable at `http://10.0.2.2:<port>/api`.)
Without it the APK uses `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`.

Install and launch:

```sh
adb install -r platforms/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.nativescript/com.tns.NativeScriptActivity
```

## 6. Build modes summary

| Target | NativeScript | JS bundle | Native configuration | Signing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iOS device | `--release` | webpack production (minified, console calls stripped) | Xcode Release, arm64, `iphoneos` | Automatic with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`, otherwise `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` |
| iOS Simulator | `--release` | webpack production | Xcode Release, `iphonesimulator` | none |
| Android | `--release` | webpack production | Gradle release | Android debug keystore |

# Notes

## Approach

- Plain NativeScript core (TypeScript) with no UI flavor (no Angular/Vue/React). All screens are built
  in TypeScript from core views (`GridLayout`, `StackLayout`, `WrapLayout`, `ScrollView`, `ListView`,
  `Label`, `Button`, `TextField`, `Image`, `ActivityIndicator`, `Frame`, `Page`); styling lives in
  `app/app.css`. The XML parser is compiled out (`__UI_USE_XML_PARSER__: false`) because no XML views exist.
- GraphQL is sent with core `Http.request` as plain `POST` JSON. Each request body contains the
  operation exactly as written in `spec/storefront.graphql` plus the fragments it spreads
  (`app/lib/operations.ts`).
- Navigation: a custom bottom tab bar (three tabs, cart badge) over three core `Frame`s, one per
  tab, so each tab keeps its own stack. The Search and Cart frames are created on first use. The tab
  bar collapses while a Product page is on top of the selected tab.
- Lazy lists: Collection and Search use the core `ListView` (UITableView / android ListView) with
  fixed-height rows; the Collection grid puts two cards in each row. A spinner row is appended while
  the next page loads. On iOS the next page is requested from the table's `contentOffset` (observed
  with KVO) when the user is within one list-height of the end. On Android the check runs from
  `itemLoading` using the last visible position.
- Images: core `ImageCache` (in-memory, at most 8 concurrent downloads) behind a small `Image`
  subclass. Images that have not loaded yet show the `surface` color. `width` is appended exactly
  as specified (1080 / 480 / 240).
- Icons: the design's SVG paths (home, search, cart, back, plus the alert, minus and plus used by
  the states and the stepper) are drawn natively as stroked vector paths (`CAShapeLayer` on iOS,
  `ShapeDrawable` on Android). No icon fonts or bitmaps.
- Log marker: `SHOPBENCH home_ready` is written with `NSLog` from a 5-line Objective-C class in
  `App_Resources/iOS/src` (NativeScript's supported way of adding native source). It is called once,
  on the first layout of Home's loaded content. NativeScript release builds strip and disable
  `console.*`, so JavaScript logging can't reach the unified log. On Android the marker goes to
  logcat (`SHOPBENCH: home_ready`).
- Endpoint: on iOS, `SHOP_API_URL` is read from the process environment at launch. On all platforms
  the same variable is also read at build time and used as a fallback; the launch environment takes
  precedence on iOS.

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **Design "See all" link** (Home, Collections header): omitted. The spec's Home description doesn't
  list it and doesn't say where it would go.
- **Empty cart "Start shopping" button** (from `States.dc.html`): included; it switches to the Home tab.
- **Error text** uses the spec's wording with a straight apostrophe: "Couldn't load products".
- **Sale styling**: the sale color plus struck-through compare-at price appears on Home best-seller
  cards, Collection cards (same card), and the Product price. Search rows and recommendation cards
  show the plain price, as drawn in the design.
- **Option pills** wrap onto more lines when they don't fit in one row.
- **Variant selection**: a pill picks the variant matching all currently selected options with that
  one value changed. If that exact combination doesn't exist, it picks the first available variant
  with that value, else the first variant with that value.
- **Add to cart failure** (network error): an alert "Couldn't add to cart. Check your connection and
  try again."; the app stays on the Product screen. `userErrors` are shown in an alert as specified.
- **Rapid stepper taps** are queued and applied in order. Each `CartLinesUpdate` computes the new
  quantity from the cart returned by the previous operation, so no tap is lost.
- **Search**: the query is trimmed; a whitespace-only field counts as empty. Scrolling the results
  dismisses the keyboard (iOS), and Return dismisses it.
- **Pagination errors**: if a later page fails, the spinner row is removed and scrolling near the
  end retries; the error state is only shown when the first page fails.
- **Product back button** is fixed over the top-left corner (it does not scroll away), so it is
  always reachable.
- **Product carousel**: a horizontal `ScrollView` with native paging (`pagingEnabled` on iOS; snap
  on release on Android). Tapping a page dot scrolls to that image. Dots appear only when there is
  more than one image.
- **Accessibility**: tappable cards and icon buttons are exposed as accessibility buttons labelled
  with their title, which is also what makes their identifiers visible to XCUITest inside table cells.
- **Request timeout**: 20 s, so an unreachable endpoint ends in the error state.
- **App icon**: the NativeScript template's default icon is kept (no custom icon). The launch
  screen is a plain white storyboard; the template's launch images were removed. Android splash
  is plain white.
- **Orientation / appearance**: portrait only, light appearance forced (`UIUserInterfaceStyle = Light`),
  iPhone only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`).

## Dependencies added

No runtime dependencies beyond `@nativescript/core`.

- `nativescript` (devDependency, CLI 9.1.1): lets the build commands in `BUILD.md` work from a clean
  checkout through `npx ns` without a global install.
- `@nativescript/ios`, `@nativescript/android` (devDependencies): the platform runtimes, pinned by
  the CLI.
- `@nativescript/webpack`, `@nativescript/types`, `typescript` (devDependencies): the standard
  NativeScript build toolchain from the official template.
- Removed from the template: `@nativescript/theme` (a CSS theme, not needed).

The in-app browser for checkout is `SFSafariViewController`, called directly through NativeScript's
native API access, so no plugin was needed. Android opens the checkout URL in the system browser
(`Utils.openUrl`), since Custom Tabs would require adding `androidx.browser`.

## Workarounds for NativeScript behavior

- `ListView.rowHeight` set before the native view exists is coerced to `auto`, which makes the iOS
  ListView measure and bind every row up front. The list re-coerces it once loaded
  (`updateEffectiveRowHeight`).
- On iOS 26, rebuilding a ListView row's native views after UITableView detaches the cell
  (which happens on every `reloadData`) intermittently threw inside UIKit
  (`-[DictionaryAdapter _resolvedMaterialWithTraitCollection:]`). The data source then returned a
  nil cell and the app aborted. The app overrides that one ListView instance method
  (`_removeContainer`) so row views keep their native views for the list's lifetime. NativeScript
  itself is not modified.

## Known limitations

- UIKit's accessibility snapshot (used by XCUITest) creates table cells for off-screen rows, so
  under UI automation more rows are built than are on screen. This is UIKit behavior. Pagination
  ignores it because it is driven by the real scroll position.
- The iOS bundle contains the `TKLiveSync.framework` that ships with the NativeScript runtime package.
  The release build does not use a dev server or live sync; the framework comes from NativeScript's
  Swift package and isn't removed (NativeScript itself is not modified).
- Android's `testID` maps to a view tag (NativeScript's behavior), not a resource-id. The benchmark
  identifiers target iOS/XCUITest.
- Every product in the mock catalog has one price across its variants, so switching options changes
  the selected variant (label, pill, cart line variant) but the displayed price stays the same. The
  price display still follows the selected variant.

  operation exactly as written in `spec/storefront.graphql` plus the fragments it spreads

  tab, so each tab keeps its own stack. The Search and Cart frames are created on first use. The tab
  bar collapses while a Product page is on top of the selected tab.

  fixed-height rows; the Collection grid puts two cards in each row. A spinner row is appended while
  the next page loads. On iOS the next page is requested from the table's `contentOffset` (observed
  with KVO) when the user is within one list-height of the end. On Android the check runs from
  `itemLoading` using the last visible position.

  subclass. Images that have not loaded yet show the `surface` color. `width` is appended exactly

The Everbloom app is built in NativeScript 9.1 (plain TypeScript, no UI framework) and every item on the spec's Done list passes. That's on the iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5) and Android emulator; I had no physical iPhone, so the signed device build is untested.

**What I verified**
- **Clean checkout:** I copied the source without generated folders and ran the BUILD.md commands. The unsigned iOS device build (arm64), the simulator build and the Android release APK all succeed. All builds are release mode with the production JS bundle.
- **Simulator, driven by Maestro (which uses XCUITest underneath):**
  - Home loads.
  - A collection scrolls to its last product (84 products, several pages).
  - All four sorts work.
  - Search returns results and pages past the first 24.
  - Options change the selected variant.
  - A recommendation opens another product.
  - Add to cart switches to Cart with badge 1. The stepper takes it to 2 and back down, and reaching 0 shows the empty state with no badge.
  - Check out opens the checkout URL in an in-app Safari view.
- **Every accessibility identifier** in the spec shows up in the XCUITest hierarchy.
- **Unreachable endpoint:** Home shows the skeleton, then the error state. Retry loads Home once a server answers at that address. `SHOP_API_URL` set at launch works, including over plain HTTP.
- **`SHOPBENCH home_ready`** appears exactly once per launch, and the app writes no other log lines.
- **Android:** the app launches on the emulator and Home loads.

**Things you should know**
- **List crash and my workaround:** NativeScript's `ListView` crashed the app every few runs on iOS 26 when the collection list reloaded (after sorting or loading the next page). I couldn't find the root cause, but the crash always happened while it rebuilt the native views of rows after a reload. My code overrides one internal `ListView` method so rows keep their native views. After that, about 40 automated runs had no crash, but it depends on a private method that a NativeScript update could break.
- **Fixed row heights:** without them, the iOS `ListView` built every row up front, which defeats the lazy-rendering requirement.
- **Pagination under UI automation:** XCUITest makes iOS build cells for off-screen rows, so in the benchmark more rows get built than are on screen. That's iOS behavior, not the app's. Because of it, the next page is requested from the real scroll position rather than when a row is built; otherwise automation would load the whole catalog.
- **Variant prices:** every product in the mock catalog has one price across its variants, so switching options changes the selection but never the price.
- **Spec gaps:** I left out the design's "See all" link because the spec doesn't say where it should go. I kept the empty cart's "Start shopping" button, which goes to Home. These and the other choices are in `NOTES.md`.
- **Dependencies:** the only addition is the NativeScript command-line tool, as a dev dependency so the build commands work without a global install. Checkout uses iOS's built-in Safari view directly, so no plugin was needed.

`BUILD.md` has the commands, build modes and tool versions; the build scripts are in `scripts/`.
